paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Before anything gets harmed, God stops everything to seal His servants. The four angels hold back the winds, and the call goes out: "Do not harm the land or sea or trees until we have placed a seal on the foreheads of the servants of our God." (Rev 7:3) So when the world feels like it's shaking, remember that God has His eye on His own, and He marks them first.

Then John sees the crowd, and it is a multitude "too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue." (Rev 7:9) Nobody gets lost in that crowd, friend. They are standing before the throne, and they have "washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb." (Rev 7:14) Their robes are white because of what Jesus did, not because of anything they scrubbed up themselves. That's the Lamb of God from John 1:29, and He's the reason the crowd is there at all.

And look at where it ends. The Lamb will be their shepherd, and "God will wipe away every tear from their eyes." (Rev 7:17) I think that is the gentlest line in the whole chapter. So hold onto that, baker. The great tribulation is real, but the Lamb gets the last word, and that's why my ovens stay ready.
